label: First laser works
detail: Theodore Maiman and Irnee d'Haenens see laser action from a ruby crystal at Hughes Research Laboratories.

label: First continuous gas laser
detail: Javan, Bennett and Herriott run a helium-neon laser at Bell Labs at 1,153 nm infrared.

label: Red helium-neon line
detail: White and Rigden at Bell Labs get the 632.8 nm red line.

label: Argon-ion laser first seen
detail: William Bridges observes argon-ion lasing at Hughes; krypton lines follow that July. These gas lasers make colored shows possible.

label: Argon-ion laser
detail: William Bridges sees the 488 nm blue line at Hughes Research Labs.

label: Rockne Krebs shows laser beams as sculpture
detail: "Sculpture Minus Object" at the Washington Gallery of Modern Art used red beams, fog and mirrors.

label: Rockne Krebs shows laser sculpture
detail: "Sculpture Minus Object" in Washington uses red beams, fog and mirrors. Other accounts date his first laser work to 1968.

label: Audio/Video/Laser at Mills College
detail: Lowell Cross, David Tudor and Carson Jeffries stage what Cross calls the first multi-color laser light show with x-y scanning.

label: Krebs files a laser art patent
detail: US patent 3,622,228, which ILDA calls apparently the first patent for laser artistic display.

label: Pepsi Pavilion opens at Expo '70
detail: A four-color krypton laser system by Cross and Jeffries runs in Osaka; Cross gives the dedication date as March 15.

label: New York regulates lasers
detail: Industrial Code Rule 50 takes effect, ahead of the US federal laser standard.

label: Laserium opens at Griffith Observatory
detail: Ivan Dryer's laser show opens in Los Angeles and runs there for nearly three decades.

label: Laserium opens at Griffith Observatory
detail: Ivan Dryer's live-played laser show begins a trial run in Los Angeles and stays 28 years.

label: Led Zeppelin photographed with lasers
detail: Three beams at Nassau Coliseum, New York - the earliest dated evidence of lasers at a rock show.

label: The Who's argon laser at Leicester
detail: A 4 W argon laser fanned through a diffraction grating at Granby Halls.

label: Moving-magnet galvo patented
detail: The design became practical with neodymium magnets in the late 1980s and reached production in 1992.

label: FDA Laser Notice 22
detail: Light shows fall under the federal standard and show producers count as manufacturers. FDA pages date it November 22 or 23.

label: Lovelight, the first automated show
detail: A planetarium laser show run from stored images and recorded control tracks, with no live player.

label: "Lovelight" runs from stored images
detail: Described by LaserFX as the first automated laser show: images drawn on a digitizing pad and stored in PROMs, control tracks on an 8-track recorder.

label: "Icarus" on steam screens
detail: Laser images projected onto steam screens over Washington DC in summer 1978.

label: Time reports FDA inspectors at light shows
detail: The Bureau of Radiological Health had told Blue Oyster Cult to adjust its show and halted a preview on the Mall in Washington.

label: Metal-ceramic ion tubes
detail: Coherent introduces Innova tubes, lifting tube life from about 1,500 hours toward 5,000.

label: Jarre plays the laser harp in China
detail: Five concerts in Beijing and Shanghai, on a harp ordered from Bernard Szajner; 218,000 attended by the artist's figure.

label: Stone Mountain laser show opens
detail: The Georgia park's mountain-side show begins; the park estimated 20 million viewers in its first 25 years.

label: Stone Mountain Lasershow begins
detail: A mountain face in Georgia becomes a laser screen about 400 ft square.

label: 21 CFR 1040.11(c) takes its current form
detail: The demonstration laser rule names Classes I, IIa, II and IIIa (50 FR 33702).

label: Pangolin's first product, Laser PC
detail: The company's About page gives 1986 for its founding; another company page says 1985.

label: Rendez-vous Houston
detail: Jarre uses downtown skyscrapers as screens; attendance is estimated at 1.3 million or 1.5 million.

label: ILDA founded
detail: The International Laser Display Association holds its first organizational meeting at Lake Tahoe, Nevada.

label: ILDA founded
detail: The International Laser Display Association holds its first organizational meeting in Lake Tahoe.

label: US manual-reset rule
detail: Class IV laser systems made after this date must need a manual reset after an interlock trip or a power loss over 5 seconds.

label: ILDA Awards begin
detail: The trade association starts its annual awards program.

label: First ILDA DB-25 specification
detail: Later superseded by the ISP-DB25 section of the ILDA Standard Projector.

label: PCAOM and the Cambridge 6800
detail: The polychromatic acousto-optic modulator and Cambridge Technology's 6800 galvo both arrive.

label: ILDA test pattern adopted
detail: The circle-in-square pattern becomes the common way to tune and rate scanners.

label: Pink Floyd tours with copper-vapor lasers
detail: The US tour carried two complete 50 W copper-vapor laser systems built by Oxford Lasers.

label: LD2000 and Phoenix
detail: Pangolin dates Lasershow Designer 2000 with QM2000 hardware to 1995; development of Phoenix Showcontroller began the same year.

label: ILDA Test Pattern revision 002
detail: The published standard sets tuning at 12,000 or 30,000 points per second.

label: ILDA Test Pattern Rev. 002
detail: The circle-in-a-square tuning frame, at 12,000 or 30,000 points per second.

label: HSE publishes HS(G)95
detail: UK guidance on display laser safety, published in October to replace note PM19 of 1980; since withdrawn.

label: O'Hagan thesis
detail: A Loughborough University PhD on entertainment laser risk finds audience scanning not acceptable as then practiced.

label: Scanners pass 50 kpps
detail: A modified Cambridge 6800 shows the test pattern at 52,083 points per second at 6 degrees.

label: ILDA Standard Projector Rev. 002
detail: Clarified signal levels and interlock on the DB-25 connector.

label: FDA Laser Notice 51
detail: Projectors may be delivered only to customers holding an approved variance.

label: Photon 999 opens at Guggenheim Bilbao
detail: Hiro Yamagata's installation projected 15 lasers onto a structure on the museum facade until December 2.

label: First OPSL ships
detail: Coherent sells a 488 nm optically pumped semiconductor laser as an ion-laser replacement.

label: Last Laserium show at Griffith
detail: "Laser Visions" plays to a sold-out dome; the observatory's timeline gives January 6, the day the building closed.

label: First multicolor laser moving head
detail: LOBO dates its ZAPHIR, a scanned laser in a moving-head fixture, to this year.

label: Plug-in RGB
detail: 5 W full-color DPSS lasers that run from a standard outlet are on offer.

label: Roger Waters adds a solid-state laser prism
detail: Five direct-diode solid-state lasers totaling over 100 W drew a rotating 3D prism above the stage.

label: FDA Laser Notice 55
detail: Streamlined yearly renewal for eligible show variances; audience scanning excluded.

label: QuickShow and FB3QS
detail: Pangolin's entry software with a USB DAC (maker's date).

label: Aquamarine festival eye injuries
detail: Festivalgoers in Kirzhach, Russia, are treated for retinal injuries after a July laser show; reports give 12, 29 or more than 30 patients.

label: Global Rainbow first shown
detail: Yvette Mattern's seven parallel laser beams, one per color of the spectrum, debut in New York.

label: Blue diodes reach hobbyists
detail: 445 nm laser diodes pulled from Casio data projectors were sold on at about $46 each, by one hobbyist's account.

label: BEYOND
detail: Pangolin's flagship show software (maker's date).

label: 18 U.S.C. 39A
detail: Aiming a laser pointer at an aircraft becomes a US federal crime under Public Law 112-95.

label: Tupac "hologram" at Coachella
detail: A 2D projection reflected off a slanted transparent film - Pepper's ghost; the vendor's CEO said it was not holographic.

label: Green diodes take over
detail: Laserworld dates the show industry's switch from DPSS green to direct green diodes to this year.

label: FB4 and IDTF Rev. 011
detail: Pangolin's network DAC (maker's date); ILDA's .ild file format reaches Revision 011 on November 16.

label: Seoul club case report
detail: Clinical Ophthalmology publishes two retinal injuries after a club laser show; both patients recovered after surgery.

label: IDN adopted
detail: ILDA members vote in Dubai to adopt the IDN Stream specification for laser data over networks.

label: 314-fixture Guinness record
detail: ER Productions ran 314 laser fixtures at 1,377 W outside the Las Vegas Convention Center during LDI.

label: Lasers as lighting fixtures
detail: PLSN describes the push to run scanned lasers from standard lighting consoles like any other fixture.

label: Mexico City swaps fireworks for lasers
detail: New Year's Eve fireworks were replaced with a concert and laser show on Reforma Avenue, for air-pollution reasons.

label: PLASA display laser guidance
detail: PLASA publishes the guide HSE now points to in place of HS(G)95.

label: 642-beam record
detail: Image Engineering set a Guinness record with 642 laser beams at Staples Center, Los Angeles.

label: Canada restricts hand-held lasers
detail: SOR/2020-124 is registered, banning hand-held lasers over 1 mW near airports and in three metro regions.

label: DGUV Information 203-036
detail: Germany's accident insurers issue the January 2021 edition of their show laser guidance.

label: MadLaser beta
detail: garageCube adds laser output to the MadMapper world.

label: FAA Advisory Circular 70-1B
detail: Current FAA guidance on outdoor laser operations; Change 1 followed on May 5, 2022.

label: 150,000 OPSLs
detail: Coherent reports more than 150,000 OPSLs in the field.

label: Stone Mountain's classic show ends
detail: The 40-year laser show is replaced by one with lasers, fireworks and drones.

label: Flagstaff replaces July 4 fireworks
detail: The Arizona city ran a free laser show set to music, citing extreme fire risk.

label: Laser-source searchlight reported
detail: Claypaky's Skylos uses a 300 W white laser source; the maker claims output equal to a 4,000 W xenon lamp.

label: 1,100-source Guinness record
detail: Verknipt ArenA at the Johan Cruijff ArenA, Amsterdam, set the current largest laser show record with 1,100 laser emission sources.

label: FAA reports 2025 laser strikes
detail: 10,994 strikes on aircraft in 2025, down 14% from 2024; the record is 13,304 in 2023.

label: FDA revises its laser import alert
detail: Import Alert 95-04, first issued in December 1997, covers laser pointers and light show projectors from listed firms.
